title: The Return of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The return of Christ means that the risen Lord Jesus will personally, visibly, and gloriously come again to judge, restore, reign, gather His people, and make all things new.
summary: The return of Christ means that the risen Lord Jesus will personally, visibly, and gloriously come again to judge, restore, reign, gather His people, and make all things new.
christFocus: Jesus is the coming King. The One who died, rose, and ascended will return in glory, defeat evil, raise the dead, judge the world, and bring His people into everlasting joy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus promised that He will come again, and the angels affirmed that the ascended Lord will return. Christian hope is not vague optimism; it is anchored in the coming of Christ.

His return will be personal, visible, glorious, and decisive. He will gather His people, judge evil, raise the dead, and bring the kingdom to its appointed fulfillment.

The return of Christ is called the blessed hope. Believers wait not for the world to save itself, but for the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.

This doctrine must be handled with sobriety, not speculation. Scripture calls believers to readiness, holiness, comfort, endurance, and longing for the Lord’s appearing.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the return of Christ, suffering can feel endless and evil can seem undefeated. His coming assures believers that history is moving toward judgment, restoration, and glory.

This doctrine gives courage to the weary church. The Lord who ascended has not forgotten His people. He will come, and every promise of God will be vindicated.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live in light of Christ’s return. Do not become obsessed with speculation or asleep in comfort. Be watchful, holy, faithful, hopeful, and ready, praying with the church, “Come, Lord Jesus.”
